title: Signature Experiment Proposal Record
body:
Overview

This record belongs to the Controlled Architecture Experiment Registry Signature Database (Signature edition), Manon's original counterpart to the public database of the same name. Experiment Proposal Record covers the following in Signature terms: states the proposed change, the reason for it, and the outcome gate it must pass. The record is written as a complete, usable file, with a demo program genuinely executed at build time and its output stored beside the code. Benchmark honesty: this database defines part of the fixed test suite for the R32 capability collection. Its target is 99% measured reliability on defined tasks (TARGET, not measured result). The comparative measurement run comes after building and is not claimed anywhere in this round.

How the Signature design works

The Signature design works like this: every experiment is registered before it runs, with its proposed change, its version, its control and treatment conditions, and its outcome gate, so results can be compared across experiments without hidden differences in setup. Applied to this record, the design means the following in practice: states the proposed change, the reason for it, and the outcome gate it must pass. The record sits at ladder rank simple in the teaching ladder, which runs simple, then compounded, then most complex, so a Signature reader can start from the simpler records and work toward this one.
